gate: 17.1 — Cross-cutting threat model and control-gap inventory

external_guidance.topic: GitHub Actions secure use; full-length commit SHA pinning
limit GitHub OIDC trust with aud/sub conditions for repository and branch
security and least-privilege permissions for agentic workflows
Top 10 for LLM and Generative AI Applications 2025

threats.threat: A pull request can satisfy the active main ruleset without any required CI status check, even though OpsLens engineering decisions rely on exact-head CI evidence before merge.
existing_controls: active Protect main repository ruleset
pull request required
review-thread resolution required
squash-only merge
linear history required
branch deletion and non-fast-forward blocked
no bypass actors
threats.residual_risk: The ruleset contains no required_status_checks rule. required_approving_review_count is 0; this is recorded separately as a governance choice, not treated by itself as the primary technical gap.
threats.recommended_action: Gate 17.2 should define the exact required CI contexts and stop at a human GitHub ruleset administration boundary for enforcement.

threats.threat: Mutable action tags or branches could change workflow code without an OpsLens commit.
existing_controls: sampled CI and AWS workflows pin actions to full 40-hex commit SHAs
repository searches found no tag-style actions/checkout@v or aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v references
threats.residual_risk: Without an automated repository-wide policy, a future workflow edit could accidentally introduce a mutable action reference.
threats.recommended_action: Add a read-only security CI invariant that rejects non-SHA external action references so the current practice becomes continuously verified.

threats.threat: actions/checkout defaults persist-credentials to true, leaving the job token available to later git commands even when the workflow does not need authenticated git after checkout.
existing_controls: explicit workflow-level GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are generally contents:read
AWS workflows add only id-token:write where OIDC is required
actions/checkout is commit-SHA pinned
threats.residual_risk: Read-only persisted credentials are still unnecessary ambient job credentials in workflows that never perform authenticated git operations.
threats.recommended_action: Gate 17.2 should set persist-credentials:false on checkout steps unless an exact workflow demonstrates a post-checkout authenticated git requirement.

threats.threat: pull_request_target or workflow_run can execute with elevated base-repository context and become dangerous when combined with untrusted checkout/execution.
existing_controls: repository searches found no pull_request_target trigger
repository searches found no workflow_run trigger
threats.residual_risk: A future workflow could introduce one of these triggers without a dedicated trust analysis.
threats.recommended_action: Continuously reject these privileged trigger types unless an explicit later ADR authorizes a narrowly reviewed use case.

threats.asset_or_boundary: GitHub Actions to AWS OIDC trust
threats.threat: A broad OIDC subject could let workflows from another repository or branch assume OpsLens AWS roles.
existing_controls: GitHub OIDC audience is exactly sts.amazonaws.com
trust subject uses immutable numeric owner/repository IDs
trust subject is exact refs/heads/main
deployment and evidence roles use the same main-only immutable subject pattern
threats.residual_risk: Future roles can drift unless the trust pattern is continuously checked.
threats.recommended_action: Retain exact aud/sub validation and add repository-wide static verification for OIDC roles/workflows in Gate 17.2.

threats.threat: The default read-only planning path assumes OpsLensEpssHistoryCoordinatorRole before branching on execute, so plan-only runs receive write/invoke authority they do not need.
existing_controls: workflow_dispatch only
main-only job condition
execute defaults false
exact confirmation phrase required before execution
coordinator role is bounded to the EPSS history workload
threats.residual_risk: Plan-only runs hold S3 write and Lambda invocation permissions. The full-backfill workflow also requests a 21,600-second session before knowing whether execution is requested.
threats.recommended_action: Gate 17.2 should separate plan/evidence credentials from execution credentials or move coordinator-role assumption into execute-only steps; long STS duration must exist only for the actual bounded execution path.

threats.threat: The retained historical workflow is intended to be non-operational after experiment IAM cleanup, but it can still assume the standing shared deployment role and perform shared-role-authorized mutations before later AgentCore-specific permission checks fail.
existing_controls: manual workflow_dispatch
explicit confirmation input
main-only job condition
AgentCore-specific standing IAM was removed after Phase 14
runtime resources are not standing
threats.residual_risk: The workflow still configures OpsLensGitHubDeployRole and publishes deployment artifacts before the AgentCore create/apply path. Historical reproducibility is therefore not equivalent to non-operational authority.
threats.recommended_action: Gate 17.2 should disable this historical workflow by default behind an explicit future-authority input and require future AgentCore re-entry to recreate a dedicated minimum principal instead of inheriting the shared deployment role path.

threats.threat: A historical cloud experiment could retain standing read authority after its value experiment completes.
existing_controls: temporary Inspector role removed and independently verified absent
retained bootstrap Terraform contains no inspector2 actions
historical workflow defaults confirm_temporary_role_exists to false
future execution requires separately recreated role authority
threats.residual_risk: A future re-entry still requires human review to avoid recreating standing authority without a new hypothesis.
threats.recommended_action: Retain the disabled-by-default historical workflow and no standing Inspector IAM.

threats.asset_or_boundary: Python dependency vulnerability discovery and update workflow
threats.threat: Known vulnerable dependencies can remain locked if the repository has no current automated dependency-update/review/vulnerability-scanning control.
existing_controls: uv.lock resolves exact dependency versions
CI runs uv lock --check and uv sync --frozen
Lambda packaging exports production requirements from the lockfile with --locked
historical Phase 2 pip-audit evidence exists for an earlier runtime snapshot
proof_refs: repository workflow search -> no active pip-audit
threats.residual_risk: No repository-configured continuous dependency update/review/code-scanning workflow is present. Account/repository platform security settings outside repository files were not observable and are not claimed disabled.
threats.recommended_action: After workflow-authority hardening, evaluate a separate Gate 17.3 for Dependabot version updates, dependency review, current vulnerability audit, and CodeQL where each control is supported for this repository.

threats.threat: Unpinned package resolution or non-deterministic archives could make deployed bytes differ from reviewed source/lock evidence.
existing_controls: production requirements exported from uv.lock with --locked
binary-only Linux-compatible dependency installation for Lambda package builders
deterministic ZIP ordering, timestamps, and permissions
artifact SHA-256/version evidence is preserved by prior deployment gates
proof_refs: Phase 2 and Phase 14 immutable artifact evidence
threats.residual_risk: GitHub artifact attestations are not currently part of the retained deployment path, but current deterministic/content-addressed controls materially reduce ambiguity.
threats.recommended_action: Revisit provenance attestations only if Phase 17/18 introduces a release/distribution requirement not already covered by deterministic SHA/version evidence.

threats.threat: A user-controlled repository URL could become SSRF, path-confusion, oversized-input, duplicate-key, or arbitrary-source authority.
existing_controls: 2 KiB request byte limit
strict UTF-8 and JSON object admission
duplicate-key rejection before ordinary mapping coercion
exact known field set
HTTPS-only github.com repository-root grammar
userinfo, port, query, fragment, percent-encoded path, and non-root repository paths rejected
raw URL is converted to validated owner/name coordinates
threats.residual_risk: No deployed public HTTP runtime is currently claimed; transport-layer abuse controls remain outside the retained application boundary.
threats.recommended_action: Retain deterministic admission. Treat rate limiting/WAF/runtime authentication as NOT_APPLICABLE until a real public transport is introduced.

threats.threat: Repository coordinates could pivot outbound requests, follow redirects, consume unbounded response bodies, or trigger adaptive retry amplification.
existing_controls: fixed api.github.com HTTPS host
GET-only transport
no redirect behavior
no adaptive transport retry behavior
bounded timeout and response byte budgets
validated path segments
exact full commit SHA required before uv.lock acquisition
strict response media type and UTF-8 JSON checks
threats.residual_risk: GitHub availability/rate limits can fail acquisition, but typed fail-closed errors preserve authority rather than broadening transport behavior.
threats.recommended_action: Retain fixed-host bounded GET semantics; do not add redirect following or arbitrary repository code execution.

threats.threat: Third-party repository text or an LLM response could alter structured query/evidence authority or inject executable inputs.
existing_controls: planner receives bounded content-free metadata rather than repository content
response byte limit
duplicate-key and exact-field admission
request-hash binding
evidence needs restricted to a closed enum
deterministic route authority validates the proposal
threats.residual_risk: Model behavior can still be wrong within the proposal grammar, so deterministic output admission remains mandatory.
threats.recommended_action: Retain proposal-only planning and never pass raw repository instructions, SQL, credentials, provider/model/tool selection, or executable content to this planner.

threats.threat: Retrieved third-party guidance can contain indirect prompt injection that attempts to become system policy or request tools/actions.
existing_controls: retrieved evidence is explicitly serialized as untrusted data
trusted instructions are frozen separately
trusted contract forbids following policy/tool/role-change commands from retrieved evidence
citation IDs are deterministic and output claims must cite admitted evidence
insufficient evidence returns a closed response
unit tests inject administrative instructions and verify they remain outside system control
threats.residual_risk: Structural separation does not prove every future model behavior is safe against every adversarial corpus; live adversarial evaluation remains a later test concern, not current authorization authority.
threats.recommended_action: Preserve the frozen trust separation; consider broader adversarial evaluation only after higher-priority workflow authority gaps close.

threats.threat: A model could propose a capability outside task scope or forge a proposal for another task, creating excessive agency.
existing_controls: proposal task_id must exactly match admitted task
capability must exist in the task-owned allowlist
authorization does not execute
executor set is closed and typed rather than a dynamic tool-name registry
typed invocation/result identities are rebound after execution
downstream exceptions become content-free failure categories
threats.residual_risk: Executor implementations still require their own least-privilege provider/runtime identities; no model proposal can waive that requirement.
threats.recommended_action: Retain deterministic authorization and typed execution/result binding. Do not move authorization into model output or protocol metadata.

threats.threat: Framework coercion or extra protocol arguments could smuggle SQL/business inputs into a supposedly reference-only tool call.
existing_controls: raw request arguments are inspected before SDK/Pydantic coercion
exact key sets are required
protocol-visible input remains content-addressed reference data
deterministic OpsLens capability admission remains authoritative
threats.residual_risk: No public/network MCP runtime is retained, so network authentication/tenant isolation is not a current runtime claim.
threats.recommended_action: Keep raw pre-coercion validation and treat network-runtime threats as NOT_APPLICABLE until deployment is explicitly authorized.

threats.threat: Duplicate keys, unknown fields, protocol identifiers, AgentCard skills, task state, or artifacts could be mistaken for OpsLens authority/evidence.
existing_controls: raw UTF-8 JSON duplicate-key rejection before coercion
exact object-key validation
strict JSON-RPC version/method/id/reference binding
code-owned reference resolution
only Message or terminal completed Task metadata is admitted
A2A identifiers and artifacts do not become business/evidence authority
threats.residual_risk: No public/network A2A peer runtime is retained, so peer network authentication and multi-tenant runtime threats are not current deployment claims.
threats.recommended_action: Retain reference-only offline admission and keep future peer deployment behind a new trust/identity decision.

threats.threat: Raw repository content, prompts, retrieved evidence, secrets, or provider output could leak into operational logs/metrics.
existing_controls: operational-telemetry:v1 is explicitly content-minimized
correlation uses content-addressed identifiers rather than source content
public-analysis tests assert inert uv.lock content does not leak into telemetry
provider failures are mapped to bounded categories in agent execution paths
threats.residual_risk: Other ingestion/runtime logs outside the Phase 10 public-analysis telemetry contract still require ordinary secret/log hygiene; this inventory found no repository-carried AWS access key pattern.
threats.recommended_action: Retain content-minimized telemetry and verify any newly introduced runtime logger against the same no-raw-content principle.

threats.threat: Unbounded prompts or output generation can create denial-of-wallet and resource exhaustion.
existing_controls: public input byte/character limits
bounded retrieval/context assembly
semantic planner max_tokens = 256
single-agent reasoning max_tokens = 96
triage reasoning max_tokens = 64
knowledge synthesis max_tokens = 2048
provider stop reasons such as max_tokens are tested and can fail closed
bounded experiments retain measured cost evidence
threats.residual_risk: There is no retained public HTTP runtime, so external per-client rate limiting, WAF, and multi-tenant quota controls are not currently applicable deployment controls.
threats.recommended_action: Retain call-level budgets. Revisit transport/client quotas only if a public runtime is actually deployed.

threats.asset_or_boundary: AWS credentials in repository and GitHub automation
threats.threat: Long-lived AWS access keys committed to source or stored as deployment credentials could be exfiltrated and reused outside intended workflows.
existing_controls: AWS GitHub workflows use OIDC rather than static AWS access keys
human administration uses temporary IAM Identity Center credentials
repository search found no AKIA access-key identifier pattern
threats.residual_risk: GitHub repository/organization secret settings are outside the observable repository content and are not claimed empty.
threats.recommended_action: Continue OIDC/Identity Center only; add secret scanning evidence later only if repository/platform configuration can be observed or enforced.

threats.threat: Stale architecture headers can cause operators/reviewers to reason about an obsolete control plane and miss retained/decommissioned runtime boundaries.
existing_controls: docs/current-state.md and docs/roadmap.md are authoritative and current through Phase 16
ADRs and immutable gate evidence preserve later-phase decisions
proof_refs: docs/architecture.md currently says baseline through Phase 9 and next Phase 10
docs/architecture.pt-br.md currently says baseline through Phase 9 and next Phase 10
threats.residual_risk: The accumulated architecture files can misrepresent phase completion even when detailed later sections exist elsewhere.
threats.recommended_action: Synchronize the architecture document headers/current-phase summary during Gate 17.1 without changing runtime behavior.

threats.threat: Single-maintainer repositories may not have an independent reviewer for security-sensitive changes.
existing_controls: PR required
review-thread resolution required
no bypass actors
squash-only linear history
threats.residual_risk: required_approving_review_count is 0 and CODEOWNERS review is not required. For the current single-maintainer portfolio context this is not automatically classified as a vulnerability.
threats.recommended_action: Revisit required independent approval when a second maintainer, production ownership model, or organizational governance requirement exists.

threats.threat: A public endpoint would require transport authentication policy, rate limits, WAF/abuse controls, quotas, and production SLO/incident controls.
existing_controls: Phase 9 deliberately closed at an application boundary
no public HTTP compute or endpoint is retained
no public runtime principal is claimed
threats.residual_risk: These controls become mandatory if a future phase actually deploys a public runtime.
threats.recommended_action: Do not invent production transport controls until a deployment requirement exists; require a fresh threat model if one is introduced.

authorized_repository_scope: reject privileged pull_request_target/workflow_run triggers unless separately authorized
set checkout persist-credentials:false where authenticated git is unnecessary
make EPSS history plan-only paths use read-only/no-write credentials
limit 21600-second EPSS coordinator session to actual execution only
disable the historical AgentCore mutating workflow by default until dedicated minimum authority is explicitly recreated
define exact required CI status contexts for main
human_or_platform_boundary: changing GitHub ruleset required status checks
not_authorized: dependency platform enablement in the same slice
